description: Figure 3 presents a circular chart illustrating the inter-annotator agreement in relation to sample-level ambiguity metrics, specifically the standard deviation and maximum ambiguity values. The chart is divided into two concentric rings: the outer ring represents the sample-level ambiguity standard deviation, segmented into four categories with corresponding percentages and standard deviation values—47.7% for Std: 0.0 (darkest blue), 38.0% for Std: 0.47 (medium-dark blue), 39.0% for Std: 0.82 (medium-light blue), and 7.0% for Std: 0.94 (lightest blue). The inner ring represents the sample-level maximum ambiguity, segmented into three categories—49.0% for Max: 1 (light blue), 14.2% for Max: 2 (medium blue), and 39.0% for Max: 3 (darkest blue). The chart visually compares the distribution of samples across these two dimensions of ambiguity, with the outer ring’s segments indicating the proportion of samples for each standard deviation level and the inner ring’s segments indicating the proportion for each maximum ambiguity level. The chart does not display any axes or numerical scales, but rather uses proportional segment areas to represent the percentage distribution of samples within each category. The figure’s caption indicates that this visualization is meant to show how inter-annotator agreement relates to the variability and maximum extent of ambiguity observed in the sample data.
